HA replication is synchronous, not asynchronous. The WAL replica maintains quorum and is not promoted; only the standby is. The standby cannot serve reporting reads.

stem: Humongous Insurance needs the configuration that protects against an entire availability zone failure with automatic zero-data-loss failover. Which option meets that goal?
choices: Zonal (same-zone) high availability
Zone-redundant high availability
A single asynchronous read replica
Point-in-time restore only
explanation: Zone-redundant HA places the standby in a different availability zone with synchronous commit and automatic failover, protecting against a full zone outage with zero data loss. Zonal HA keeps both nodes in one zone, so a zone failure takes both down. An asynchronous read replica can lose data on failover. PITR is recovery after an outage, not automatic failover.

stem: Litware Media stores 40,000 product embeddings in Azure Managed Redis and needs exact nearest-neighbor recall with the simplest index configuration. Which RediSearch vector index type fits both needs?
choices: FLAT, an exact brute-force index
HNSW with a high EF_RUNTIME
IVFFlat with many probes
DiskANN with a large search list
explanation: FLAT performs an exhaustive brute-force scan that returns exact nearest neighbors and needs no graph tuning, which suits a small dataset requiring exact recall. HNSW is approximate even with a high EF_RUNTIME. IVFFlat and DiskANN are not RediSearch vector index types.

stem: In an Azure Managed Redis RediSearch HNSW vector field, what does EF_RUNTIME control?
choices: The build-time candidate list size
The query-time candidate list size, trading recall against latency
The maximum number of results returned
The maximum number of outgoing edges per node
explanation: EF_RUNTIME is the size of the query-time candidate list; raising it improves recall at the cost of higher query latency. The build-time candidate list is EF_CONSTRUCTION. Result count is set by the KNN K value. Edges per node is the M parameter.

stem: A developer at Trey Research is defining an Azure Managed Redis HNSW vector field. Which two parameters are set at index creation time rather than at query time?
choices: EF_RUNTIME and K
M and EF_CONSTRUCTION
K and DISTANCE_METRIC only
EF_RUNTIME and M
explanation: M (edges per node) and EF_CONSTRUCTION (build candidate list) are HNSW build-time parameters set when the index is created. EF_RUNTIME and K are supplied per query. DISTANCE_METRIC is set at creation but K is per query. Pairing EF_RUNTIME with M mixes a query-time and a build-time parameter.

stem: VanArsdel runs a product recommender on Azure Managed Redis that must search only items where category is shoes and then rank those by vector similarity. Which approach uses RediSearch correctly?
choices: A hybrid query that combines the tag filter with KNN, such as (@category:{shoes})=>[KNN 10 @v $blob AS score]
A pure KNN query, then discard non-shoes results in the client
A FLAT index scan over every vector with no filter
A numeric RANGE query with no vector clause
explanation: RediSearch hybrid search applies the metadata filter to narrow the candidate set and then runs KNN vector ranking in a single query. Filtering in the client wastes work and can return too few shoes. Scanning all vectors ignores the category constraint. A range query with no vector clause performs no similarity ranking.

stem: Southridge Video wants to cut LLM cost and latency by reusing prior answers when a new prompt means the same thing as an earlier one, even if the wording differs. Which pattern does this describe?
choices: Semantic caching keyed by prompt embedding similarity
Exact-key string caching of prompt text
Output caching of static HTTP responses
Write-behind caching of database rows
explanation: Semantic caching embeds prompts and returns a cached completion when a new prompt is similar enough to a prior one, reducing cost and latency. Exact-key caching only reuses byte-identical prompts. HTTP output caching serves static content, not LLM completions. Write-behind caching defers database writes and is unrelated to prompt reuse.

stem: An architect at Nod Publishers plans to use vector search on Azure Managed Redis. Which statement about the RediSearch module is correct?
choices: Modules cannot be added after the cache is created, so RediSearch must be enabled at provisioning
RediSearch can be added to an existing cache at any time
RediSearch is available on the Flash Optimized tier
RediSearch works only with the OSS clustering policy
explanation: You must enable RediSearch when creating the cache because modules cannot be added afterward. Adding a module to an existing cache is not supported. RediSearch is not available on Flash Optimized. RediSearch requires the Enterprise clustering policy, not OSS.

stem: Alpine Ski House is enabling RediSearch vector search on Azure Managed Redis. Which clustering and eviction combination does RediSearch require?
choices: OSS clustering policy with allkeys-lru eviction
Enterprise clustering policy with NoEviction eviction
OSS clustering policy with NoEviction eviction
Enterprise clustering policy with volatile-ttl eviction
explanation: RediSearch requires the Enterprise clustering policy and the NoEviction eviction policy. The OSS clustering policy is not supported for RediSearch, and any eviction policy other than NoEviction risks evicting indexed data, so allkeys-lru and volatile-ttl are invalid here.

stem: Best For You Organics uses a cache-aside pattern and needs a read immediately after an application-controlled write to return the fresh value. What write path achieves this?
choices: Write only to the cache and let it flush to the database later
Write to the database, then invalidate or update the cache entry so the next read repopulates it
Rely on the cache TTL to expire the stale entry eventually
Write to the cache first, then write to the database asynchronously
explanation: In cache-aside, the system of record is the database; writing there first and then invalidating or updating the cache guarantees the next read reflects the new value. Writing only to the cache risks data loss and diverges from the database. Waiting for TTL leaves a stale window. Cache-first asynchronous writes are write-behind and can serve stale or lost data.

choices: ivfflat.probes
hnsw.ef_search
ivfflat.lists
diskann.l_value_is
explanation: ivfflat.probes controls how many lists are scanned at query time; raising it improves recall at the cost of speed. hnsw.ef_search and diskann.l_value_is tune different index types. lists is a build-time WITH option, not a runtime SET parameter.

stem:
Complete the CREATE INDEX so the HNSW build considers 200 candidates while constructing the graph. Which option fills the blank?

```
CREATE INDEX ON items
USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (m = 32, ________ = 200);
```
choices: ef_construction
ef_search
l_value_ib
lists
explanation: ef_construction is the build-time dynamic candidate list for HNSW graph construction. ef_search is a query-time setting, not a build option. l_value_ib belongs to DiskANN. lists belongs to IVFFlat.

stem:
Complete the pgvector query that generates the query embedding in-database with the azure_ai integration. Which function fills the blank?

```
SELECT id, title
FROM knowledge_base
ORDER BY content_vector <=> azure_openai.________('embeddings', $1)::vector
LIMIT 5;
```
choices: create_embeddings
generate_embeddings
embed_text
get_vectors
explanation: azure_openai.create_embeddings calls the deployed Azure OpenAI embeddings model and returns a result that casts to vector. generate_embeddings, embed_text, and get_vectors are not functions exposed by the azure_ai integration.

stem:
Complete the RediSearch schema so the HNSW vector field uses cosine similarity for text-embedding-3-small vectors. Which value fills the blank?

```
FT.CREATE idx ON HASH PREFIX 1 doc:
  SCHEMA v VECTOR HNSW 6
  TYPE FLOAT32 DIM 1536
  DISTANCE_METRIC ________
```
choices: COSINE
L2
IP
DOT
explanation: COSINE is the RediSearch distance metric matching cosine-similarity embedding models such as text-embedding-3-small. L2 is Euclidean distance and IP is inner product, which do not match the cosine model here. DOT is not a valid RediSearch DISTANCE_METRIC value.

stem:
Complete the RediSearch query so it returns the 10 nearest vectors with a query-time candidate list override. Which keyword fills the blank?

```
FT.SEARCH idx "*=>[________ 10 @v $blob EF_RUNTIME 150 AS score]"
  PARAMS 2 blob "..." SORTBY score DIALECT 2
```
choices: KNN
ANN
TOPK
NN
explanation: KNN is the RediSearch vector query keyword that returns the top K nearest neighbors. ANN, TOPK, and NN are not RediSearch vector query keywords.

stem: A workload at First Up Consultants uses Azure's built-in PgBouncer in its default pool mode. Which two features do not work reliably in that mode? (Select two.)
choices: Session-level advisory locks
LISTEN and NOTIFY pub-sub messaging
Protocol-level prepared statements when max_prepared_statements is above 0
Single-statement autocommit SELECT queries
Ordinary multi-statement transactions
explanation: Advisory locks and LISTEN/NOTIFY both require a persistent server connection, which transaction pooling does not guarantee because the connection returns to the pool after each transaction. Protocol-level prepared statements work once max_prepared_statements is above 0. Single-statement SELECTs and ordinary transactions are fully supported in transaction pooling.

stem: Graphic Design Institute is provisioning Azure Managed Redis for vector search with RediSearch. Which two configuration choices are required? (Select two.)
choices: Enterprise clustering policy
NoEviction eviction policy
OSS clustering policy
allkeys-lru eviction policy
Flash Optimized tier
explanation: RediSearch requires the Enterprise clustering policy and the NoEviction eviction policy so indexed data is not evicted. The OSS clustering policy is not supported for RediSearch. allkeys-lru can evict indexed keys. Flash Optimized does not support RediSearch.

stem: An engineer at Munson's Pickles wants to create a pgvector index on an empty table and populate it afterward. Which two index types can be built on an empty table because they have no training step? (Select two.)
choices: IVFFlat
HNSW
DiskANN
A B-tree over the vector column
A BRIN over the vector column
explanation: HNSW and DiskANN build graphs incrementally with no training step, so they can be created on an empty table and populated as data arrives. IVFFlat trains list centroids on existing data, so it needs data first. B-tree and BRIN indexes do not support vector distance operators.

stem: On Azure Managed Redis, which two of the following are valid RediSearch vector DISTANCE_METRIC values? (Select two.)
choices: COSINE
IP
DOT_PRODUCT
MANHATTAN
HAMMING
explanation: RediSearch supports L2, COSINE, and IP as vector distance metrics, so COSINE and IP are both valid. DOT_PRODUCT, MANHATTAN, and HAMMING are not RediSearch vector distance metric values.

stem: Lucerne Publishing guards a hot cache key with a single-flight lock to prevent a cache stampede when the entry expires. Which two statements describe correct single-flight behavior? (Select two.)
choices: Exactly one request recomputes the value while the others wait or serve a stale copy
Every concurrent request recomputes the value independently to maximize freshness
A lock key acquired with SET NX lets only one caller rebuild the entry
The cache is disabled for all keys during the miss window
Using GET then SET as two separate commands guarantees only one caller wins
explanation: Single-flight lets one request rebuild the value while others wait or serve stale, and SET with NX is the atomic primitive that grants the lock to exactly one caller. Independent recomputation by every request is the stampede itself. Disabling the whole cache is overbroad. GET followed by SET is two non-atomic steps, so several callers can pass the check and win the race.
